definition: A portion of data deliberately excluded from training and used exclusively for evaluating a model's generalization performance.
details: Held-out sets (a broader term encompassing validation and test sets) are fundamental to honest machine learning evaluation, providing a check against a model simply memorizing its training data.
story: Think of a referee whose job is to be completely honest about who touched the ball last. Before trusting a machine, someone has to measure how good it really is — fairly and honestly. It is the exam that separates “it sounds good” from “it actually is good”. What gets measured is what actually gets better. That shared ruler is Held-Out Set.
